data.name: Star Tactics Redux
data.detailed_description:
Star Tactics is a hardcore turn-based strategy and tactics game full of spacefleet battles.
30+ hours of gameplay, infinite randomized battles, huge campaign with different ways of completion. Experience infinite tactical situations and outsmart the tricky AI using dozens of ships and special abilities.

Do expect fierce battles with dozens of ships involved, infinite amount of challenging tactical situations, tough decisions of how to compose your fleets and pure joy when destroying an enemy ship. Because battles are tough.



Main features:
  • Turn-based tactical gameplay with top-down perspective;
  • Campaign featuring large-scale fleet battles. 30 missions, different ways to compose your fleet to increase replayability and involve thinking;
  • Skirmish mode - infinite randomized battles. Level up your Commander and access new ships;
  • Special abilities like missile or torpedo strike, afterburner, forcefield, U-turn and other awesomeness;
  • 36 ships from smallest Scout to tremendous Command Dreadnought;
  • Ship variants with different stats, weapons and abilities. Total of 60+ different units;
  • 9 weapons of different tactical roles which projectiles shine like little stars;
  • Advanced AI: ships avoid missiles, fly from the most vulnerable side, set targets according to priority (capitals target capitals, fighters target fighters) and take into account their most effective side, firepower-wise;
  • Different map objects like damaging gas field, nebulas to hide and make an ambush, asteroids and mine fields. Battles are really diverse;
  • Interesting, skill-based achievements with meaningful rewards;
  • Rare visual style with holographic vibe;
  • Great visuals overall: a lot of VFX, particles and postprocess aligned to make the game look astounding;
  • Carefully handcrafted UI and user experience;
  • Music by X3 and X-Rebirth composer.

reviews.review:
Star Tactics Redux is a turn-based space combat strategy game that puts careful planning ahead of reflexes. Developed and published by Devil's Dozen Games, it focuses on commanding fleets across tactical battlefields where positioning, ship selection, weapon ranges, and special abilities can determine whether an engagement ends in victory or disaster. Its presentation is relatively straightforward, but underneath the holographic visuals is a surprisingly involved combat system aimed primarily at players who enjoy methodical strategy.

Fleet building is one of the strongest parts of the experience. There are 36 basic ships alongside numerous variants, bringing the overall selection to more than 60 vessels. These range from small and maneuverable craft to much heavier capital ships and dreadnoughts. The variety encourages players to think about fleet composition instead of automatically selecting the biggest ships available. Different vessels fulfill different purposes, and combining their strengths is often more useful than relying on a single class of powerful warship.

Combat unfolds through turns, giving plenty of time to examine the battlefield and decide how each vessel should move or attack. Nine weapon types contribute to the tactical variety, while abilities including missile attacks, torpedoes, forcefields, afterburners, and rapid turning maneuvers create additional possibilities. Orientation also matters because ships may be more effective when attacking or defending from particular directions. This makes maneuvering meaningful rather than simply being a way of moving closer to an enemy.

Enemy behavior adds another interesting dimension. Opposing ships can respond to incoming missiles, choose targets according to their battlefield roles, attempt to exploit vulnerable directions, and maneuver to make better use of their own weapon systems. This gives battles a more deliberate rhythm and punishes careless decisions. Charging directly into the enemy without considering formations or firing positions can quickly become costly, particularly during larger engagements where numerous ships must be managed at once.

The campaign contains 30 missions and provides the main progression structure. New ships and commander development help create a sense of advancement while gradually giving players more options for constructing their fleets. The game advertises more than 30 hours of campaign content, although actual playtime will naturally depend on tactical skill and willingness to experiment. Outside the campaign, randomized skirmishes extend the game's longevity by providing battles that can be approached with different fleet combinations and strategies.

Battlefields are not always empty stretches of space either. Asteroids, minefields, gas clouds, and nebulas introduce environmental considerations that can alter otherwise straightforward engagements. Dangerous areas can restrict movement, while other features may provide opportunities to conceal ships or prepare an ambush. These environmental elements are particularly effective when combined with the game's emphasis on positioning because they force players to consider where a battle is taking place instead of focusing exclusively on enemy statistics.

Visually, Star Tactics Redux uses a colorful holographic style that resembles a futuristic tactical display. Glowing ships, weapon effects, particles, and other visual effects give battles a distinctive science-fiction appearance without attempting photorealism. The style fits the strategic nature of the game because ships remain relatively easy to identify from the overhead perspective. Its age and independent origins are noticeable in some aspects of the interface and overall presentation, but the aesthetic has enough personality to prevent the experience from feeling completely generic.

The biggest obstacle is accessibility. This is deliberately a strategy-heavy experience, so players expecting rapid real-time battles or an action-oriented space shooter may find its pacing too restrained. Learning how the different ships, weapons, abilities, and environmental features interact takes time. There is also less emphasis on cinematic storytelling and character-driven drama than players might expect from larger space adventures. The attraction is primarily the tactical system itself, and enjoyment depends heavily on whether planning fleet engagements sounds appealing.

Steam Deck compatibility is currently not officially rated by Valve, so it should be regarded as Unknown or Unverified rather than Verified or Playable. The game's modest Windows system requirements suggest that raw performance is unlikely to be its biggest obstacle, but the lack of an official Steam Deck compatibility rating means controller behavior, interface readability, and Proton compatibility cannot be guaranteed. Players specifically purchasing it for handheld use should therefore expect that some configuration or experimentation may be necessary.

Star Tactics Redux ultimately works best for players who enjoy taking their time, studying tactical possibilities, and experimenting with different combinations of ships. The large vessel roster, weapon variety, special abilities, environmental hazards, campaign missions, progression systems, and randomized skirmishes provide a respectable amount of strategic depth. Its presentation is modest and its slower pacing will not suit everyone, but the underlying fleet combat offers plenty to explore for fans of turn-based science-fiction strategy.

Rating: 8/10
